title: Offline map correction walk
summary: A safe daylight walk for correcting offline maps, blocked paths, water points, steep slopes, gates, and hazards before the next evacuation or supply run.
content: Core sequence: 1) Walk only in daylight with a return time and a second person knowing the route. 2) Mark obstacles, dogs, locked gates, flooded points, shade, water, and places with phone signal. 3) Use simple symbols and update the date so old hazards are not treated as current. 4) Return before tiredness changes judgment; the correction walk is not a rescue mission. Stop point: Do not use offline map correction walk to enter a restricted, contaminated, structurally unsafe, or officially closed area. Main warnings: Do not continue offline map correction walk after the stop signs named in the steps appear. Do not let urgency turn offline map correction walk into a task done alone without a visible check-in.
materials: small route card for each correction
water and closed shoes for the walker
